subject: Renewal: adding EU + APAC reserved pools — throughput & failover details
messages:
From: Anna Lindberg <anna.lindberg@fastretail.co>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:17:00Z
Subject: Renewal — scope: add EU + APAC reserved pools and throughput targets

Hi Jonas —

We're coming up on our 12/15 renewal and want to lock in capacity for the next 12 months. Usage has grown faster than we forecasted; Traffic by region (30% US / 50% EU / 20% APAC) means we need separated reserved pools for EU and APAC to meet latency requirements and compliance constraints.

High-level asks:
- Add dedicated EU reserved pool sized to sustain ~450 QPS peak (text generation workload) with p95 latency target <= 150ms for typical L1 prompts.
- Add dedicated APAC reserved pool sized to sustain ~180 QPS peak with p95 <= 220ms.
- Transparent failover behavior: EU primary with APAC as hot standby (no cross-region cold start >500ms for key storefronts).
- Contract amendment to reflect additional monthly reserved units and a one-time onboarding fee.

Can you confirm feasibility and what you would propose for pool sizes, throughput guarantees, and any latency SLO language we should expect in the amendment?

Thanks —
Anna
Anna Lindberg
Head of Platform Engineering, FastRetail

Subject: Re: Renewal — scope: add EU + APAC reserved pools and throughput targets

Anna — thanks for the clear ask and the retention policy. This is definitely doable; I want to propose a short workshop so we can size pools against your real token mix and peak window. Quick notes / clarifying questions before we meet: 

1) Can you share 7-day peak QPS for generation and the breakdown by prompt length (short/median/long)? Even estimated percentiles are fine.
2) Do you expect active cross-region traffic routing for customers (i.e., APAC customers hitting EU when APAC is down), or do you prefer regional sticky routing with fallback?
3) Are you comfortable with a two-tier SLA: availability for reserved pools (monthly uptime) + p95 latency targets by region? We commonly do 99.95% uptime for reserved pools plus region-specific p95 latency objectives.

Tentative technical proposal (subject to workshop and ops validation):
- EU reserved pool: 10x H100-equivalent reserved GPUs (balanced for short and long sequences) targeting sustained 500 QPS headroom for burst protection.
- APAC reserved pool: 4x H100-equivalent reserved GPUs targeting sustained 200 QPS.
- Failover: fast-stale KV cache strategy + regional prefix caching to reduce cold starts. Cross-region fallback configured as fail-open with retry backoff; documented RTO for cross-region failover should be <= 1 minute for non-critical paths and <500ms for edge routing of small queries (we'll enumerate exceptions).

I'll loop in Karthik and Laura to validate the H100-equivalent counts and whether we should model on A100/H100 or aggregated vGPU capacity. Can we schedule a 45-minute sizing call tomorrow or Thursday?

—Jonas

Looping in ops/infra notes — fyi for Jon and Anna: 

We did a quick simulation based on their stated 50% EU / 20% APAC split and assumed median prompt lengths of 45 tokens (short bursts) and heavy tails to 2k tokens. Preliminary capacity mapping:
- EU pool: 8 H100-equivalent reserved slots configured with autoscale headroom to burst to 12 for seasonal peaks. Expected sustained throughput ~420–520 QPS depending on batching.
- APAC pool: 3 H100-equivalent reserved slots with burst to 5. Expected sustained throughput ~160–220 QPS.

Latency guarantees we can commit in the amendment (draft recommendation):
- EU: p95 inference latency <= 150ms for standard prompt mix at <= 85% sustained utilization; p99 <= 400ms (with documented exceptions for long-run prompts).
- APAC: p95 <= 220ms at <= 80% sustained utilization; p99 <= 700ms.

Failover model:
- Primary routing: regional sticky with health checks.
- Hot-standby: APAC will have warm prefixes and a reduced KV cache refresh window so that on failover we get <1s token-level response for cached prefixes and a median cold-start delta of ~250–600ms depending on sequence length.
- RTO and customer-visible failover: operational RTO target is 5 minutes for full region failover; for critical storefront endpoints we can prioritize routing rules to meet <1s impact for critical user flows (extra engineering + runbook).

We should present these numbers as ranges in the contract, add an SLA table, and include an onboarding runbook and the one-time onboarding fee. I've attached a short ops checklist (internal).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
